A '''group''' is a [[set]] closed under one binary operation, with some special properties by definition.

== Formal definition ==

Let $G:|G| \ge 1$ be a set, and $*$ a [[binary operation]] defined over $G$.

If $\forall a,b,c \in G$:

* $(a*b)*c=a*(b*c)$ ('''associativity''')
* $\exists id \in G: a*id=a=id*a$ ('''identity''')
* $\exists (a') \in G, a*a'=id=a'*a$ ('''inverse''')
*

then $(G,*)$ is a '''group'''.

If furthermore $a*b=b*a$ ('''commutativity'''), group $(G,*)$ is said to be '''abelian'''.

<blockquote>
The smallest group is $(\{id\},*)$, where $*$ can be e.g., $\cdot$.
</blockquote>

<ref>{{#cite:Q2230}}</ref>

== Examples ==

For each of the $G$ below, $(G,\cdot)$, where $\cdot$ takes its usual definition, is a group:

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! $(G,*)$
! Note
|-
|| $(\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0\},\cdot)$
| Abelian group of rational numbers with addition, $id=1$
|-
|| $(\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0\},\cdot)$
| Abelian group of non-zero rational numbers with multiplication, $id=1$
|-
|| $(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\},\cdot)$
| Abelian group of non-zero real numbers with multiplication, $id=1$
|-
| | $\{(a,b)|a,b \in \mathbb{R},\, a,b \neq 0\}$
| Abelian group of non-zero real 2D vectors with vector multiplication, $id=(1,1)$
|}

'''Counterexamples''':

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! $(G,*)$
! Why $(G,*)$ is not a group?
|-
| $(\mathbb{Q},\cdot)$
| $a=0 \in \mathbb{Q}: \nexists a' \in \mathbb{Q},a*a'=1$
|}
